title: Canary dependency upgrade review scratch
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratch for rolling a small dependency bump (onnxruntime 1.16 -> 1.17) through serving runtime. This is a working checklist / set of heuristics — not the final runbook. Notes to self while pairing with Tomas on 2025-02-14.

Background:
- Reason: 1.17 has a kernel path that removes an unaligned memcpy in our CPU fallback path; measured ~2.5% token latency improvement on model-x bench.
- Risk: some macOS/arm64 wheels historically flaky; but our infra uses linux-x86_64 GPUs + CPU fallback. Still, native op changes could affect numerical outputs for edge-case kernels (float16 -> float32 casts).
- Scope: only bump runtime dependency and associated conformance test updates. No model topology changes.

Quick gating heuristics (what I check before approving a tiny PR):
- CI green: unit + integration tests for serving-runtime, slow integration, and model-smoke. If flaky but consistent across commits, pause.
- Latency baseline: perf CI contains median p50/p95/p99 for token latency on model-x and chat-y. Acceptable: p99 <= previous_p99 * 1.03 and p50 <= previous_p50 * 1.01.
- Output fidelity: run deterministic prompt set (promptset/fidelity-2025-02) and compare diffs. Accept if changes <= 0.2% tokens different AND no new hallucination patterns flagged in eval harness.
- Memory: RSS / GPU memory footprint within 5% of baseline under the same workload.
- Binary artifact checksums: wheel signature matches CI build; ensure portable linux wheel used (no mac tags).

Pre-merge checklist (local + PR comments):
- [ ] Confirm CI matrix uses the exact wheel built in the PR (not upstream wheel) — add a job to build wheel and publish to ephemeral registry.
- [ ] Run local smoke: 
  - docker run -e MODEL=model-x --rm infra/serving:local-debug ./run-smoke.sh --seq 512 --requests 50
  - Verify no crashes, KV cache stays populated, and p50 latency roughly same.
- [ ] Run conformance (fast subset): python tests/conformance/test_ops_subset.py::test_attention_op -k onnxruntime
- [ ] Run deterministic fidelity eval: ./eval/run_fidelity.sh --prompts promptset/fidelity-2025-02 --out out/fidelity-before.json; merge PR; run again and diff.
- [ ] Add PR description with explicit rollback plan and quick revert PR link template.
- [ ] Tag SRE oncall in the PR and request a +canary label.

Canary rollout plan (small change, conservative schedule):
- Stage 0: internal dev cluster (0% external traffic) — 10 replicas for 1h, synthetic workload (model-x chat trace). Monitor logs for exceptions.
- Stage 1: 1% traffic via smart routing for 2h, compare token latency and error rate with control; SLOs: error rate increase < 0.2pp, p99 delta <= +3%.
- Stage 2: 10% traffic for 4h if metrics good.
- Stage 3: 50% for 2h.
- Stage 4: full roll.
Notes: use automatic rollback if error rate > 0.5pp or latency p99 > +6% for more than 10 minutes.

Metrics and dashboards to watch (where I jot quick IDs):
- perf.token_latency.model-x.p50/p95/p99 (console route: perf -> model-x -> token-latency)
- infra.errors.serving-runtime.exception_rate
- memory.rss.serving-instance
- gating: request.error_rate.rerouted, routing.latency
- logsearch query: "TypeError OR NaN OR segfault OR onnx" in last 60m

Smoke commands I run locally (copyable):
- build wheel: python -m build -s -w; twine upload --repository-url https://pypi-internal.redwood/dev dist/*
- run local container (uses internal wheel): docker-compose -f docker/dev-compose.yml up --build
- quick load test (50 parallel clients): locust --headless -u 50 -r 5 -t 2m -f loadtests/send_tokens.py --host http://localhost:8080

Potential refactor ideas triggered by this change (brainstorm):
- Short-term: isolate memcpy path behind a feature flag so we can A/B test kernel variants without wheel changes. Would let us test new memcpy-less path on prod builds.
- Mid-term: add a compact binary op validation harness that runs a subset of ops with seeded random tensors comparing outputs between runtime versions (fast, low-cost). Could catch subtle numerical diffs early.
- Long-term: abstract kernel selection into a small plugin interface so runtime can pick optimized kernels at runtime based on telemetry (sequence length histogram). Avoid heavy wheel churn.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Does quantized-ops test matrix cover our T4 fallback paths? Tomas to confirm by 2025-02-15.
- Should we pin to a specific onnxruntime commit for Dedicated customers? SLA implications if we ship wheel with non-deterministic op layout. Ask product about contractual freeze window.
- Is there any metric that correlates numerical tiny diffs with downstream hallucination? We currently only measure token diffs; need an eval tie-in.

Post-merge follow-ups (TODO list):
- [ ] Add an automated fidelity-run in nightly CI that records token-diff history (artifact: s3://redwood-ci/fidelity-history/onx-1.17).
- [ ] Update release notes with regression testing summary and rolling schedule.
- [ ] Start an RFC for 'runtime kernel plugin' (skeleton doc in docs/arch/kernel-plugin-rfc.md).
- [ ] Sweep: confirm model owners for top-5 customer-facing models are notified (email template below).

Quick email template to notify owners:
Subject: Canary rollout — onnxruntime 1.17 (serving runtime)
Hi <owner>,
We plan a staged canary for onnxruntime 1.17 targeting serving-runtime next week. Expected p99 delta small but please review the attached deterministic prompt set results. If you see anything concerning, reply and we'll pause rollout.
Planned schedule: Stage 1 (1%) Tue 10:00 PST, Stage 2 (10%) Tue 14:00 PST.
Aria + Tomas

Notes-to-self style: short snippets I left while pairing:
- "If fidelity diff spikes only for single prompt: likely nondeterministic seed -> don't rollback globally; mark prompt and re-run with seed fixed."
- "Edge-case: model-y uses custom CUDA kernel - confirm not affected."
- "If p99 spikes but p50 stable, think about outlier requests (large seq) — check sequence-length histogram in last hour."

End of scratch. Will make a cleaned runbook if canary behaves. Save this as working notes and move final steps to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/runbooks/once-stable.
